grounding.quote: It names the semitone counts of the common intervals and the major/minor triad recipes.

Build a major and a minor triad from a r.check_prompt: Which note is the third of a C minor triad?
Build a major and a minor triad from a r.counter: Changing the root moves the whole triad, but the third still decides the quality; build it from G to hear the same shape.
Build a major and a minor triad from a r.criterion: Both triads share the root and fifth; lowering the middle note is the whole difference.
Build a major and a minor triad from a r.criterion_short: Both triads share the root and fifth.
Build a major and a minor triad from a r.explanation: Both triads share the root and fifth; only the third moves, which is why the third carries the quality.
headings: Stack both triads from one root
Lower the third, keep the fifth
Build a major and a minor triad from a r.intent: Teach the triad recipes and check both spellings.
Build a major and a minor triad from a r.practice: From C, stack a major third and a perfect fifth for the major triad, then lower the middle note for the minor.
Build a major and a minor triad from a r.practice_short: From C, stack a major third and a perfect fifth.
Build a major and a minor triad from a r.why: A triad is the chord you will find in every song analysis later, so the recipe is learned on one root first.

Count the semitones in a major third and.check_prompt: How many semitones are in a perfect fifth?
Count the semitones in a major third and.counter: If you count from the wrong start note the number still adds up, which is why you say the start note and the interval together.
Count the semitones in a major third and.criterion: From C, the fifth note arrives after the same four-semitone step plus three more.
Count the semitones in a major third and.criterion_short: From C, the fifth note arrives after a four-semitone step.
Count the semitones in a major third and.explanation: Counting semitones turns an interval from a feeling into a number you can check at the keyboard.
Count the semitones in a major third and.explanation_short: Counting semitones turns an interval into a number you can check.
headings: Check the count at the keyboard
Count the semitones in a major third and.intent: Teach the semitone count and check recall of the two numbers.
Count the semitones in a major third and.practice: Start on C, count four semitones to E, and say the interval name out loud before you play it.
Count the semitones in a major third and.practice_short: Start on C and count four semitones to E.
Count the semitones in a major third and.why: Every interval you name in this course is a semitone count, so this number is the unit the rest of the course measures with.

Distinguish the two common thirds by sou.check_prompt: Which interval is three semitones wide?
Distinguish the two common thirds by sou.counter: Naming the interval before you look at the keys keeps the ear honest; naming it after is just reading the keys.
Distinguish the two common thirds by sou.criterion: The darker, lower interval is the one whose middle note is flattened; name it before checking the keys.
Distinguish the two common thirds by sou.criterion_short: The darker, lower interval is the one whose middle note is flattened.
Distinguish the two common thirds by sou.explanation: The third decides whether a triad sounds major or minor, so the ear has to hear the difference before the theory helps.
Distinguish the two common thirds by sou.explanation_short: The third decides whether a triad sounds major or minor.
Distinguish the two common thirds by sou.intent: Teach the sound difference and check the learner can name it.
Distinguish the two common thirds by sou.practice: Play C to E, then C to E flat, and hum each interval back before naming it.
Distinguish the two common thirds by sou.practice_short: Play C to E, then C to E flat.
Distinguish the two common thirds by sou.why: The two thirds are the whole difference between a major and a minor sound, so the ear is trained before the letters are.

Use the circle of fifths to name the cho.check_prompt: A song uses C, G, A minor and F. Which key is it in?
Use the circle of fifths to name the cho.counter: A song that never settles on its home chord is still analysable, because the circle still shows the neighbouring chords it borrows from.
Use the circle of fifths to name the cho.criterion: The home chord is the one the song resolves to; name it before the key.
Use the circle of fifths to name the cho.criterion_short: Name the home chord before the key.
Use the circle of fifths to name the cho.explanation: The circle shows which chords belong together, so a song's chord list becomes a key and a set of functions.
Use the circle of fifths to name the cho.explanation_short: The circle shows which chords belong together.
headings: Find each root on the circle
Use the circle of fifths to name the cho.intent: Teach the circle as a song-analysis tool and check one mapping.
Use the circle of fifths to name the cho.practice: Write the song's chords, find each root on the circle, and mark the home chord before naming the key.
Use the circle of fifths to name the cho.practice_short: Write the song's chords and find each root on the circle.
Use the circle of fifths to name the cho.why: The circle is the map from chords to a key, and the home chord is the landmark you find first on that map.

evidence_criteria: Names which third was played and why
objectives.title: Distinguish the two common thirds by sound

prerequisite_assumptions: The learner can find middle C on a keyboard or piano app.
The learner has no formal theory training and is not assumed to read music.
shape.terminal_performance: Read intervals, triads and the circle of fifths, and explain how a chord is built.
shape.through_line: Each unit turns a sound into a number and then a number into a name: semitones first, then the thirds, then the triads, then the circle that places every chord of one real song.

units.goal: Name an interval from its semitone count and sound.
units.title: Intervals on the keyboard

units.goal: Build a triad from the circle and use it on a real song.
units.title: Triads and the circle of fifths
